transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-09-15 10:00am PT | Duration: ~60 min
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendoza (AcuityAI - Dir ML), Priya Shah (AcuityAI - SRE), Jared Klein (AcuityAI - CTO)

--- Summary (auto) ---
Ethan: quick alignment on goals and scope; run customer scripts through our harness, compare streaming vs non-streaming, validate p99 latency and cost numbers, decide dedicated vs hosted for pilot.

00:00 Ethan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm ethan from redwood, we'll keep this tight, objective is to scope the poc benchmarks and get your scripts running in our harness.
00:22 Carlos: thanks, yea we wanna see realistic numbers against our live workload, uh samples is fine, but prefix caching and session behaviour is important.
00:40 Maya: quick q for priya — do you run streaming responses in prod or mostly non-streaming?
00:50 Priya: mostly streaming for end-user chat, but batch non-streaming for back-office classification jobs, so both matter, and we do long context in some flows.
01:10 Ethan: perfect, so we'll plan to run two passes: streaming emulation and non-streaming bulk. We'll need your inference scripts and a small dataset sample, ideally 1k requests.
01:30 Carlos: can you emulate our concurrency profile? we have spikes to ~300 rps during peak, steady at ~40.
01:45 Maya: yes we can, the harness supports shaping traffic. question about kv cache — your workloads have heavy session reuse, so KV caching will matter for costs.
02:05 Priya: correct, session affinity and kv cache hit ratio is typically ~65% for us.
02:20 Maya: good to note, that will change throughput significantly.
02:32 Jared: on security we need SSO and audit logs for the pilot - that's non-negotiable.
02:42 Ethan: we can provide audit logs and SSO via SAML, we'll include the security docs.
02:57 Carlos: timeline wise, we want results within two weeks of handing over scripts. realistic?
03:10 Ethan: aim for 10 business days from receipt, assuming no infra blockers.
03:22 Maya: practical questions: do you want us to run on hosted first or dedicated? for throughput testing dedicated gives cleaner numbers but hosted shows integration friction.
03:40 Priya: we'd prefer hosted initial run to validate compatibility then hop to dedicated for scale.
03:55 Ethan: sounds reasonable. we'll do hosted smoke + dedicated benchmark.
04:10 Carlos: success criteria — p99 latency < 400ms for short responses, p50 < 120ms, throughput to handle 300 rps with 95% success, and cost target sub $X per 1M tokens (we'll provide target).
04:35 Maya: noted — we'll record p50/p95/p99, token cost, and model quality delta versus your baseline.
04:50 Priya: quality checks — how do you handle regen/temperature differences in bench? we need deterministic comparisons.
05:05 Maya: harness supports deterministic seeds and can run same prompts across model variants; we'll capture outputs for a sample eval.
05:20 Carlos: ok, also streaming vs non-streaming matter: streaming adds overhead but reduces user-perceived latency, how do you benchmark that?
05:35 Ethan: we simulate stream chunks and measure time-to-first-byte (TTFB) and end-to-end. we'll report both TTFB and full-generation latencies.
05:50 Jared: what about gRPC vs REST? our infra prefers gRPC for lower overhead.
06:02 Maya: harness supports both; if you give us your client stubs we can run your exact client flows.
06:15 Carlos: we'll share a dockerized client for exact parity.
06:28 Ethan: perfect. on model variants — do you have a preferred open model or are you testing multiple?
06:40 Carlos: primary model is an open Llama-variant quantized to 4-bit, but we also have a larger non-quant model for quality control.
06:55 Maya: that aligns with our recommended profiles; we'll run quantized and fp16/32 comparators.
07:10 Priya: network constraints — during peak we see 1gbps egress, and we have strict egress controls in our VPC. if we do dedicated on your infra we need a private link.
07:30 Ethan: noted, for private/dedicated we can set up VPC peering or private link. we'll include network runbook.
07:45 Carlos: for measurement, we also care about cold-start for long contexts — KV cache warm vs cold. can you do both?
07:58 Maya: yes, harness supports cold-run and steady-state runs; we'll report both.
08:15 Ethan: quick recap of data we'll need from you: 1) ~1k sample queries with metadata (session ids), 2) your client runner docker, 3) quality baseline dataset and thresholds.
08:32 Carlos: will provide by monday. one ask — does the harness support websocket streaming?
08:44 Maya: yes, websocket and http chunked streaming both supported, though websocket has slightly different metrics collection.
09:00 Priya: latency SLO — can you instrument host-level metrics as well (GPU utilization, nvlink, memory)?
09:15 Maya: we can collect GPU metrics (util, mem, temp) via the agent on dedicated; hosted has limited host-level telemetry but we still provide per-request timing.
09:30 Jared: when you say "cost per 1M tokens", does that normalize for batching differences?
09:40 Ethan: yes, we'll report unit economics for each configuration, factoring batching, quant, and cache hits.
09:52 Carlos: can you show an example harness run? a quick walkthrough would help.
10:05 Maya: sure, high level: harness has three components — runner (drives clients), collector (metrics), and scorer (quality diffs). you mount your runner docker and we map traffic onto the runtime under test.
10:25 Carlos: any special instrumentation for streaming?
10:32 Maya: we capture chunk latencies and TTFB, and we can replay user think times. there's some noise in TTFB for streaming but we'll run many samples.
10:45 Priya: will you run load generator from our VPC or from your hosted infra? we prefer inside our VPC to avoid egress variance.
10:58 Ethan: for dedicated we'll run inside VPC; hosted runs will be from our region - we'll note network noise.
11:12 Carlos: about harness setup — how much effort on our side to dockerize the runner?
11:20 Priya: we can do it, but need a template.
11:28 Maya: we'll send a runner template and an example config. should be ~1-2 hours to wrap your client.
11:40 Jared: on timelines, if we hand off scripts monday, can you complete hosted smoke in 3 days and dedicated benchmark within 10?
11:56 Ethan: yes that matches earlier. deliverables: harness repo, runbook, required env vars, and results dashboard.
12:10 Carlos: any blockers around auth for private data? we need KMS integration and token scoping.
12:22 Maya: for private/dedicated we support customer KMS and token scoping; we'll need a short onboarding to configure keys.
12:35 Priya: also need SOC2 type II docs and data retention policy.
12:42 Ethan: we'll attach security pack (SOC2, ISO, data retention, audit logs).
12:55 Carlos: ok, one more — are you able to do per-route autoscaling and fallback to cheaper model variants? we may want a multi-tier routing policy in prod.
13:10 Maya: yes, our routing supports policy-based fallback by latency/cost/region; we'll demo that in the console if helpful.
13:25 Ethan: ok quick recap and next steps — sending harness + template by 9/17, customer shares scripts+dataset by 9/20, we schedule a run week of 9/22 with SE involved.
13:40 Carlos: sounds good. thanks all.

--- Action items (transcript) ---
Ethan: share harness repo + runbook (due 2026-09-17)
Maya: config recommendations (batching, quantization, dedicated size) (due 2026-09-18)
Carlos: provide 1k sample queries, dockerized runner, quality thresholds (due 2026-09-20)
